key_insight: FARL enables safe offline-to-online fine-tuning for real-world manipulation by detecting intervention-requiring failures and autonomously triggering a learned self-recovery policy, allowing continued online learning without human rescue.
problem_solved: Real-world online fine-tuning of RL policies is blocked by intervention-requiring failures (e.g., spills, breakage). FARL addresses the safety and practicality gap by preventing or recovering from such failures during exploration so offline-trained policies can be safely adapted online.
method: Failure-aware monitoring: learn or estimate failure risk / detect IR failures online (uncertainty or classifier) to flag dangerous states before catastrophic outcomes.
Self-recovery policy: a dedicated recovery behavior trained (or distilled) to safely restore the robot from failure-prone states without human intervention.

Conservative offline-to-online updates: risk-aware policy updates and safe-exploration constraints that fall back to recovery/offline policy when risk is high, enabling sample-efficient, safe adaptation.
impact: Enables practical deployment of RL for delicate manipulation by reducing human interventions and catastrophic events during online fine-tuning, improving safety, robustness, and real-world sample efficiency.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: offline dataset → base policy + failure monitor → online loop with risk check → recovery policy fallback
Sequence illustration: detected risky state → trigger recovery → resume learning (before/after frames)
Bar/line chart: comparison of intervention incidents and success rates (baseline RL vs FARL) across tasks
Icon set: robot arm, hazard/warning, shield (safety), and dataset/learning symbol
paper_title: Failure-Aware RL: Reliable Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Self-Recovery for Real-World Manipulation
paper_authors: Huanyu Li, Kun Lei, Sheng Zang, Kaizhe Hu, Yongyuan Liang
